tables.name: segmentation_rules
tables.purpose: Stores each merchant-defined segmentation rule with its conditions, target tag, version counter, and soft-delete timestamp.

columns.name: conditions
columns.purpose: Structured rule conditions: { min_spend_cents: number|null, min_order_count: number|null, country_codes: string[]|null }; all fields optional; all present conditions are ANDed together during evaluation

columns.name: target_tag
columns.purpose: The Shopify customer tag written to every customer that satisfies all conditions in a run

columns.name: version
columns.purpose: Monotonically incremented by 1 on every successful update; snapshotted into rule_runs at run creation time

columns.name: deleted_at
columns.purpose: Non-null when the rule has been soft-deleted; soft-deleted rules are excluded from list queries and may not be run

tables.name: rule_runs
tables.purpose: Tracks every execution of a segmentation rule, recording its lifecycle state, the rule version applied, and the outcome summary.

columns.name: rule_id
columns.constraints: NOT NULL REFERENCES segmentation_rules(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
columns.purpose: The segmentation rule this run belongs to; RESTRICT prevents deleting a rule that has historical run records

columns.name: rule_version_snapshot
columns.purpose: The rule version number captured at the moment the run was created, enabling audit of which conditions were applied

columns.name: newly_tagged_count
columns.purpose: Number of customers newly tagged during this run; null until the run reaches completed state

columns.name: failure_reason
columns.purpose: Human-readable error message recorded when the run transitions to failed; null for successful runs

columns.name: completed_at
columns.purpose: Non-null once the run reaches completed or failed state

transitions.trigger: start_run recipe claims the run immediately after inserting it
transitions.action: sql_claim UPDATE rule_runs SET status='running' WHERE id=? AND status='pending'

transitions.trigger: all matching customers successfully tagged and count recorded
unrecoverable error during customer fetch or tag application

admin.purpose: Return a paginated list of all non-deleted segmentation rules ordered by most recently updated first.

admin.purpose: Create a new segmentation rule with the supplied name, conditions, and target tag.
Overwrite an existing non-deleted rule's name, conditions, or target tag and increment its version.

Trigger an immediate synchronous execution of a segmentation rule; returns the final run outcome after all tagging is complete.
Return the current status and result summary of a specific run.
Return a paginated history of executions for a given rule ordered most recent first.

list_rules.description: Return a paginated list of non-deleted segmentation rules ordered by updated_at DESC.

steps.purpose: Clamp page to minimum 1 and page_size to range 1-100 with default 20
Clamp page_size
Calculate OFFSET from page and page_size
Count total non-deleted rules for pagination metadata
steps.template: SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS total FROM segmentation_rules WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

steps.purpose: Fetch page of non-deleted rules ordered by updated_at DESC
steps.template: SELECT id, name, conditions, target_tag, version, created_at, updated_at FROM segmentation_rules WHERE deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT ${safePageSize} OFFSET ${offsetVal}

steps.purpose: Audit list-rules request
Return paginated rules list

postconditions: Rules are ordered by updated_at DESC.
total reflects the full unpaged count of non-deleted rules.
edgeCases: If no rules exist, rulesRows is [] and total is 0 — return empty array with total 0.
If page exceeds total pages, rulesRows is [] — return empty array with correct total.

create_rule.description: Validate inputs and insert a new segmentation rule row with version=1.

steps.purpose: Sanitize rule name by stripping null bytes
Sanitize target tag by stripping null bytes and trimming whitespace
Reject request if name or target_tag is empty after sanitization

body.error: name and target_tag are required and must be non-empty

steps.purpose: Build validated conditions object with all fields defaulting to null when absent
steps.expression: { min_spend_cents: (conditions.min_spend_cents != null ? Math.round(Number(conditions.min_spend_cents)) : null), min_order_count: (conditions.min_order_count != null ? Math.floor(Number(conditions.min_order_count)) : null), country_codes: (Array.isArray(conditions.country_codes) && conditions.country_codes.length > 0 ? conditions.country_codes.map(c => String(c).toUpperCase().trim()) : null) }

steps.purpose: Insert the new rule row with version=1
steps.template: INSERT INTO segmentation_rules (name, conditions, target_tag, version) VALUES (${safeName}, ${safeConditions}, ${safeTag}, 1) RETURNING id, version

steps.purpose: Audit rule creation
Return new rule id and initial version

postconditions: Exactly one row inserted into segmentation_rules with version=1 and deleted_at=NULL.
conditions JSONB is stored with normalized country_codes in uppercase.
edgeCases: conditions object may omit some or all filter keys — missing keys are stored as null, not as errors.
min_spend_cents must be stored as an integer (already in cents from the client); if the client sends a float, it is rounded.

update_rule.description: Overwrite a non-deleted rule's fields and atomically increment its version.

steps.purpose: Sanitize rule name
Sanitize target tag
Reject if name or tag is empty

body.error: name and target_tag are required and must be non-empty

steps.purpose: Build validated conditions object
steps.expression: { min_spend_cents: (conditions.min_spend_cents != null ? Math.round(Number(conditions.min_spend_cents)) : null), min_order_count: (conditions.min_order_count != null ? Math.floor(Number(conditions.min_order_count)) : null), country_codes: (Array.isArray(conditions.country_codes) && conditions.country_codes.length > 0 ? conditions.country_codes.map(c => String(c).toUpperCase().trim()) : null) }

steps.purpose: Atomically update the rule and increment version, guarding against acting on a deleted rule
steps.template: UPDATE segmentation_rules SET name=${safeName}, conditions=${safeConditions}, target_tag=${safeTag}, version=version+1, updated_at=now() WHERE id=${ruleId} AND deleted_at IS NULL RETURNING id, version

steps.purpose: Return 404 if no row was updated (rule not found or already deleted)
Audit rule update
Return updated rule id and new version

postconditions: version is incremented by exactly 1 per call.
updated_at is refreshed to current timestamp.
Deleted rules return 404 and are not modified.
edgeCases: Concurrent updates to the same rule are serialized by the UPDATE row lock; each caller gets the version after their own write.
If a run starts between an update and the next run trigger, the run captures the new version.

delete_rule.description: Soft-delete a segmentation rule by setting deleted_at so it no longer appears in listings or can be triggered.

steps.purpose: Set deleted_at on the rule, guarding against double-delete or missing rule
steps.template: UPDATE segmentation_rules SET deleted_at=now(), updated_at=now() WHERE id=${ruleId} AND deleted_at IS NULL RETURNING id

steps.purpose: Return 404 if rule was not found or already deleted
Audit rule deletion
Confirm deletion

postconditions: Rule row has deleted_at set to a non-null timestamp.
All rule_runs rows referencing the rule remain intact (ON DELETE RESTRICT preserved history).
Subsequent calls to delete the same rule return 404 without error.
edgeCases: A rule with an active running run is still soft-deletable; the running run continues to completion with its own version snapshot and is not interrupted.
Attempting to start a new run for a deleted rule returns 404 in the start_run recipe.

start_run.description: Synchronously execute a segmentation rule: insert a pending run, claim it as running, bulk-fetch all Shopify customers, evaluate conditions, tag matching customers one by one, then record the completed or failed outcome.

steps.purpose: Fetch the rule to verify it exists, is not deleted, and to read its current conditions and version
steps.template: SELECT id, name, conditions, target_tag, version FROM segmentation_rules WHERE id=${ruleId} AND deleted_at IS NULL

steps.purpose: Abort with 404 if rule not found or deleted
Extract conditions object from rule row
Extract target tag from rule row
Capture rule version snapshot at run-creation time
Insert a new run record in pending state capturing the rule version snapshot
steps.template: INSERT INTO rule_runs (rule_id, rule_version_snapshot, status) VALUES (${ruleId}, ${ruleVersionSnapshot}, 'pending') RETURNING id

steps.purpose: Extract run id from inserted row
Atomically transition run from pending to running; guards against double-execution if two requests race
steps.template: UPDATE rule_runs SET status='running', started_at=now() WHERE id=${runId} AND status='pending' RETURNING id

steps.purpose: Record run start
Bulk-fetch all customers with the fields required for rule evaluation across all pages
steps.query: query FetchCustomersForSegmentation($cursor: String) { customers(first: 250, after: $cursor) { nodes { id amountSpent { amount } numberOfOrders defaultAddress { countryCodeV2 } tags } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }

steps.purpose: Evaluate each customer against all rule conditions and exclude those already carrying the target tag; treat missing spend/order count as zero; treat missing country as non-matching for country conditions
steps.expression: allCustomers.filter(c => { const spendCents = Math.round(parseFloat(c.amountSpent?.amount ?? '0') * 100); const orderCount = parseInt(c.numberOfOrders ?? '0', 10); const countryCode = c.defaultAddress?.countryCodeV2 ?? null; const alreadyTagged = Array.isArray(c.tags) && c.tags.includes(targetTag); if (alreadyTagged) return false; const spendOk = conditionsObj.min_spend_cents == null || spendCents >= conditionsObj.min_spend_cents; const orderOk = conditionsObj.min_order_count == null || orderCount >= conditionsObj.min_order_count; const countryOk = !Array.isArray(conditionsObj.country_codes) || conditionsObj.country_codes.length === 0 || (countryCode != null && conditionsObj.country_codes.includes(countryCode)); return spendOk && orderOk && countryOk; })

steps.purpose: Record evaluation result before tagging begins
Apply the target tag to each matching customer via individual Shopify tagsAdd mutations
Use the GID already present on the customer node from the Shopify response
Add the target tag to this customer in Shopify
steps.mutation: mutation TagsAdd($id: ID!, $tags: [String!]!) { tagsAdd(id: $id, tags: $tags) { node { id } userErrors { field message } } }

steps.purpose: Record per-customer tag success
Count newly tagged customers
Transition the run to completed and record the newly tagged count
steps.template: UPDATE rule_runs SET status='completed', newly_tagged_count=${newlyTaggedCount}, completed_at=now() WHERE id=${runId} AND status='running'

steps.purpose: Record run completion
Return completed run summary to the admin panel

postconditions: Exactly one rule_runs row exists per invocation, transitioning pending→running→(completed|failed).
newly_tagged_count equals the number of customers that did not previously carry the target tag and matched all conditions at the time of the bulk fetch.
Customers already carrying the target tag are neither re-tagged nor counted.
rule_version_snapshot on the run row matches the version of segmentation_rules at the moment the run was inserted.
edgeCases: The codegen MUST wrap steps 9 through 14 (shopify_query through the completed sql_update) in a single try/catch block; on any caught error the handler MUST execute: UPDATE rule_runs SET status='failed', failure_reason=<err.message truncated to 1000 chars>, completed_at=now() WHERE id=${runId} AND status='running'; then return HTTP 500 with body { run_id: runId, status: 'failed', newly_tagged_count: null, failure_reason: err.message }.
If the Shopify customers query returns zero nodes (empty store), matchingCustomers is [], newlyTaggedCount is 0, and the run completes normally.
A customer with null defaultAddress has no countryCode; if the rule specifies country_codes, that customer is excluded without error.
A customer with null or '0.0' amountSpent is treated as spendCents=0 so spend threshold conditions evaluate correctly.

tagsAdd userErrors for a single customer causes the entire run to fail via the try/catch wrapper, not silently skip that customer — the failure_reason records the offending customer GID and userErrors message.

If two concurrent start_run requests are received for the same rule, both insert separate run rows and proceed independently; the second run's deduplication reflects the tag state after the first run's writes at the time of its own customer fetch.

get_run_status.description: Return the current status, outcome summary, and completion timestamp for a single run.

steps.purpose: Fetch the run record by id
steps.template: SELECT id, status, newly_tagged_count, failure_reason, completed_at FROM rule_runs WHERE id=${runId}

steps.purpose: Return 404 if run not found
Return run status and outcome fields

postconditions: Response reflects the current committed state of the run row at query time.
edgeCases: A run in running state returns status='running' with newly_tagged_count=null and completed_at=null; the admin panel should continue polling.
A stalled run (status='running' with started_at more than a reasonable elapsed time ago) is visible here and can be detected by the merchant or a recovery procedure.

list_runs.description: Return a paginated history of rule run records for a given rule ordered by started_at DESC.

steps.purpose: Clamp page to minimum 1
Clamp page_size to 1-100 with default 20
Calculate OFFSET
Count total runs for the given rule for pagination metadata
steps.template: SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS total FROM rule_runs WHERE rule_id=${ruleId}

steps.purpose: Fetch page of run records for the rule ordered by started_at DESC
steps.template: SELECT id, rule_id, rule_version_snapshot, status, newly_tagged_count, failure_reason, started_at, completed_at FROM rule_runs WHERE rule_id=${ruleId} ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT ${safePageSize} OFFSET ${offsetVal}

steps.purpose: Audit list-runs request
Return paginated runs list

postconditions: Runs are ordered by started_at DESC.
total reflects the full unpaged count of runs for the given rule_id.
Runs for soft-deleted rules are still returned as long as the rule_id matches.
edgeCases: If no runs exist for the rule yet, runRows is [] and total is 0.
The ruleId is not validated for existence in this recipe; if a non-existent rule_id is passed, countResult is 0 and runRows is [] — the response is an empty page, not a 404.

platformGaps.gap: Shopify provides no batch mutation to add tags to multiple customers in a single API call.
platformGaps.mitigation: The start_run recipe issues one tagsAdd mutation per matching customer inside a for_each loop; the run record in rule_runs tracks overall progress and outcome via the workflow state machine.
platformGaps.uxImplication: For rules matching large customer sets the admin panel should display the run as in-progress until the status polling endpoint confirms completed or failed; estimated duration grows linearly with the number of matching customers.

platformGaps.gap: The handler executes synchronously within a single HTTP request; very large customer bases may exhaust the request timeout before all tagsAdd mutations complete.
platformGaps.mitigation: The try/catch wrapper in start_run marks the run as failed with a descriptive failure_reason when the request is interrupted, leaving the run_runs row in an auditable failed state that the merchant can observe via list_runs and retry.
platformGaps.uxImplication: The admin panel should warn the merchant that runs on stores with more than approximately 5,000 matching customers may time out and require a retry.

uxExpectations.admin: The admin panel should present a two-panel layout: a rule list on the left showing name, target tag, version, and last-updated date with Create/Edit/Delete actions, and a run history panel on the right scoped to the selected rule showing each run's status badge (pending/running/completed/failed), newly_tagged_count, rule version applied, and started_at timestamp. The Run Now button should be disabled while any run for that rule is in running state and should display a spinner; on completion it should flash the newly_tagged_count inline so the merchant sees the result without navigating away.

edgeCases: A rule_runs row stuck in running state beyond a reasonable elapsed time (e.g. started_at older than 10 minutes) indicates a crashed handler; the list_runs and get_run_status routes expose this state and a recovery procedure should execute UPDATE rule_runs SET status='failed', failure_reason='stalled: handler crashed before recording outcome', completed_at=now() WHERE status='running' AND started_at < now() - interval '10 minutes'.

The merchant edits a rule (incrementing its version) and immediately triggers a run before the update response returns; the start_run recipe reads the rule version at INSERT time so the run's rule_version_snapshot always reflects the exact conditions active at that moment, not a stale snapshot.

Two concurrent start_run requests for the same rule both insert separate pending rows and both claim their own row via sql_claim WHERE status='pending'; they proceed independently and each produces its own completed run row, so the second run's deduplication excludes customers already tagged by the first run only if the first run's tagsAdd mutations committed before the second run's graphqlPaginate completes.

Soft-deleting a rule while a run is in running state does not interrupt the run; the run continues to completion using its own ruleVersionSnapshot and the rule_runs FK (ON DELETE RESTRICT) is not violated because the rule row remains present with deleted_at set.

A segmentation_rules.conditions JSONB column with all three filter keys null is a valid rule that matches every customer not already carrying the target tag; the evaluate compute expression treats all null conditions as non-restrictive.

country_codes in conditions are stored and compared as uppercase ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 codes (e.g. 'US', 'CA'); the create_rule and update_rule recipes normalize incoming codes to uppercase, and the evaluate expression compares against the normalized stored values — mismatches due to case differences are prevented at write time.
